sovereign_country.strategic_role: 非洲第一大金融枢纽、辐射南部非洲关税同盟（SACU）商贸

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Vertical Industrial ERP and Customer Relationship Software

stage_1.jurisdiction_name_en: South Africa (National jurisdiction; unitary company-law regime; no sub-state company register; City of Johannesburg/Tshwane only for municipal licensing)
stage_1.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Roman-Dutch common law overlayered by English company-law principles, constitutional supremacy, and statutory regulation; Companies Act 71 of 2008 is modelled on English/Australian corporate law
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BIT: Agreement between the Republic of South Africa and the People's Republic of China on the Promotion and Protection of Investments (signed 1997; in force 1998)
Multilateral: SACU Treaty 2002; SADC Protocol on Trade (2000); SADC Protocol on Finance and Investment (2006); AfCFTA Agreement (ratified by South Africa, deposited 2019)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, ss 14 (incorporation), 15 (MOI), 19 (legal personality), 66 (board), 70 (officers); Companies Regulations, 2011, Chapters 4 and 5 (forms and eCoR procedure)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), a public entity operating under the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR 15.1) submitted through the CIPC eCoR online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital or escrow account requirement for private companies; shares are allotted as stated in the MOI and the solvency and liquidity test applies before distributions
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the incorporation documents filed under Companies Act 71 of 2008, namely the Notice of Incorporation and Memorandum of Incorporation lodged with CIPC, are hereby ratified; the subscribers named in the Notice of Incorporation subscribe for and are allotted the initial ordinary shares set out opposite their names in the share register; the registered office stated in the MOI is adopted as the company’s legal seat and physical address; the first directors named in the MOI are appointed; and [Name] is appointed Managing Director, [Name] Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] Company Secretary, with full authority to execute banking, hiring, licensing, and tax registration matters on behalf of the company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve company name or adopt registration number
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the CIPC company and name database, submit a name reservation application and prescribed fee, and obtain approval. If no name is used, the company may be incorporated solely by its registration number.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or opposed, file a name reconsideration or dispute response within the statutory period, or select an alternative name; a registration-number company does not require name approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Memorandum of Incorporation and statutory consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Applicant preparer / company legal advisor; filing subsequently with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the MOI using the prescribed model, including share classes, director authorities, quorum rules, and the registered office. Complete the Notice of Incorporation and obtain signed consents from each proposed director and the company secretary.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as company secretary
Identity documents of first directors and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any inconsistencies between the MOI and the Notice of Incorporation; revise the MOI by written amendment before filing, or resubmit a clean signed set if CIPC issues a query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File incorporation documents and obtain certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into eCoR, attach the Notice of Incorporation and MOI, pay the processing fee, and submit for verification. When no exclusions are detected, CIPC issues the Certificate of Incorporation; the company exists from that date.
required_dossiers: Approved name reservation or registration number notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC queries the application, remedy the stated defect and resubmit within the indicated period; if the application is rejected, file a fresh application with corrected documentation and, where necessary, apply for reconsideration of the MOI.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt first board resolutions and statutory registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors and company secretary; records maintained at registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting, approve the pro-forma board resolution, allocate shares to subscribers, and issue share certificates. Open and maintain registers of members, directors, the company secretary, and beneficial interests.
required_dossiers: Approved minutes of the first board meeting
Register of directors and the company secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any governance omission by passing a subsequent board resolution under the Companies Act; file a Notice of Change of Registered Office or Officers (CoR 22.1) if a registered detail changes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation tax, labour, and municipal clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (eFiling); Department of Employment and Labour; local municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for income tax, VAT, PAYE, and UIF via SARS eFiling within 21 business days of incorporation or commencement of business, whichever is earlier. Register as an employer and for the Compensation Fund. Obtain a zoning certificate, fire clearance, and certificate of occupation for the registered premises if they are physically occupied.
required_dossiers: SARS tax registration application and supporting documents
UIF and Compensation Fund registration applications
Certificate of occupancy / structural installation clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, pay any prescribed late filing penalties and maintain proof of exemption; municipal objections to zoning or occupancy may be cured by an internal appeal to the local planning tribunal or by leasing compliant commercial premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 6201 (software programming and cloud ERP/CRM); general policy oversight by the Department of Communications and Digital Technologies and the dtic, but no industrial manufacturing licence is triggered
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no dedicated sectoral operating licence is required for a vertical cloud software business under South African law; customary municipal zoning and business premises compliance apply

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) under the National Environmental Management Act (NEMA) and its provincial/local competent authorities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — administrative office and cloud software activity do not constitute a listed activity under the Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations, 2014; no environmental authorisation is required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial point-source emissions or VOC thresholds apply; sanitary and domestic effluent must comply with municipal trade effluent bylaws and the National Water Act, while waste, including e-waste, must be handled by registered waste service providers under the National Environmental Management: Waste Act, 2008

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance issued by the local fire department; structural and electrical compliance with the National Building Regulations (SANS 10400) evidenced by a municipal certificate of occupancy; workplace compliance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993, including a clean electrical certificate of compliance and emergency evacuation plan

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); portal: SARS eFiling at https://www.sarsefiling.co.za (official site: https://www.sars.gov.za)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A South African incorporated (Pty) Ltd is automatically allocated an Income Tax Reference Number at CIPC incorporation; activation is completed through SARS eFiling 'Register for Tax' using the RAV01 form, confirming the public officer (mandatory under s246 Tax Administration Act). VAT registration is made on form VAT101: compulsory once taxable supplies exceed R1,000,000 in any 12-month rolling period, or voluntary if taxable supplies exceed R50,000 in any 12-month period (VAT Act s23). Foreign-owned subsidiaries must submit the acceptance-of-appointment letter for the public officer, certified memorandum of incorporation, and local physical address proof; a SARS excise/customs code is separately obtained if the entity exports goods. SARS issues a VAT vendor number, PAYE number and a single reference number; confirmation is usually issued within 21 business days after submission of the RAV01/VAT101 through eFiling.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; resident (Pty) Ltd is taxed on worldwide income at 27% corporate income tax (as applicable to years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023); no pass-through regime available to companies; dividend distributions attract 20% dividends tax with withholding by the entity; branch profits remitted by a foreign-owned South African branch are subject to an additional 15% branch profits tax; capital gains are included at 80% (21.6% effective rate for companies).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. Applicable elections for a South African (Pty) Ltd: (a) VAT grouping election (s50 VAT Act) allowing related entities to be treated as a single vendor; (b) two-method input apportionment election for mixed taxable and exempt supplies (s17(1) VAT Act); (c) election under s9D(9)/s9D(2A) for the high-tax exemption or low-tax exclusion of Controlled Foreign Company income; (d) s24I election to treat exchange differences on foreign currency obligations on a translation basis; (e) s11D R&D tax incentive pre-approval election with the Department of Science and Innovation, and (f) s12B renewable energy allowance election. Hybrid mismatch adjustments (s23M and s8E/s8EA) are mandatory, not elective, and require full disclosure in the corporate income tax return.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: R1,000,000 (compulsory once value of taxable supplies exceeds R1,000,000 in any 12-month period; voluntary registration if taxable supplies exceed R50,000 per annum; a foreign e-services supplier under s47A isn't relevant to this locally incorporated (Pty) Ltd whose supply of ERP/CRM cloud services to non-residents is zero-rated or standard-rated resident cloud services at 15%).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance/CTC or digital stamping is currently imposed by SARS. Electronic tax invoices are lawful under s20(4) VAT Act if the invoice contains all 15 prescribed particulars (including identifier 'tax invoice', supplier VAT number, dated transaction, description, price, VAT amount) and ensures authenticity of origin, integrity of content and legibility. SARS has announced a voluntary National e-Invoicing Standard aligned with the ITU/UN standard; pilot filings and an API-based clearance framework are being developed, but until a SARS Notice is gazetted, no statutory obligation exists for API pre-clearance, e-stamping or real-time validation of B2B invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to: (1) exported goods under s11(1)(a) where the goods are removed from South Africa within the prescribed period and documentary proof of export is retained; and (2) services supplied to non-residents under s11(2)(k) — including hosted ERP/CRM, software licensing and technical support — where the recipient is a non-resident who is outside South Africa at the time the services are rendered, the services are not directly connected to land or movable property situated in South Africa, and the services are not supplied to a resident acting as intermediary. The vendor must retain contracts, bank records and support logs demonstrating offshore consumption; simple invoicing to a foreign address without proof of payment from abroad or service performance outside South Africa is insufficient to support 0% treatment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: SARS Customs Export Declaration (SAD500/DA550) electronically submitted and released through the SARS Customs Single Administrative System
Bill of Lading, Airway Bill or Cargo Carrier Waybill evidencing physical departure from the South African port of exit
Commercial invoice/tax invoice in the name of the non-resident buyer indicating 'Zero-rated export' and VAT registration number
Inward Remittance Certificate (COT3) or bank confirmation evidencing receipt of foreign currency/offshore settlement within 180 days
Service supply contract, IP licensing chronology and technical performance log demonstrating supply to a non-resident outside South Africa for s11(2)(k) treatment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS reconciles zero-rated VAT claims against Customs export declarations, banking data and eFiling VAT201 disclosures. Insufficient documentation causes the zero-rating to be rejected with output VAT at 15% assessed plus interest (TAA ss89 and 90), and an understatement penalty under TAA s222-223 of up to 150% of the shortfall for intentional tax evasion (10% substantial understatement; 25% no reasonable grounds; 50% gross negligence; 150% intentional evasion). Fraudulent zero-rating claims attract additional tax of up to 100% of the tax amount under VAT Act s44, possible criminal prosecution (TAA s234, imprisonment up to 5 years) and disclosure in SARS public defaulters lists. Overstated refunds also trigger a 10% penalty under VAT Act s39(2) and a VAT refund fraud flag that restricts future eFiling refunds for up to 3 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through its Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933, the Exchange Control Rulings, and the Currency and Exchanges Manual for Authorised Dealers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The ZAR is a managed-float currency with a substantially liberalised current account: cross-border payments for software subscriptions, hosting services, royalties, and trade settlements may be executed through an Authorised Dealer without prior FinSurv approval once supporting invoices and balance-of-payments (BOP) declarations are provided. The capital account remains exchange-control-regulated: non-resident equity capital may be injected freely and must be reported to the Authorised Dealer, while non-resident shareholder loans above the ZAR 3 million aggregate threshold require prior FinSurv approval, and outward capital remittances (dividends, capital reductions, share buy-backs, loan repayments to non-residents) require SARS Tax Compliance Status, CIPC beneficial-ownership proof, and Authorised Dealer adjudication. For the software exporter, profit remittance hurdles are low: a (Pty) Ltd with non-resident shareholders may declare dividends and remit them through an Authorised Dealer subject to a valid SARS tax compliance certificate and an auditable distributable reserve; the practical hurdles are documentary (FICA customer due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and underlying contract evidence) rather than quantitative rationing, and no discriminatory conversion restriction is applied to current-account transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (CoR 37.1) with annual declaration of shareholding
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of ZAR 110 (~USD 6) per annual return plus compliance notice; two consecutive years of delinquency triggers deregistration under s82 Companies Act 2008; reinstatement requires a court application

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register Annual Confirmation (CIPC BO declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed simultaneously with the annual return; every share transfer must update the register within 7 days of change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure of directors to submit or update the BO register is an offence under s33(5) Companies Act 2008, as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 2024; directors face a fine up to ZAR 450,000 (~USD 25,000) or imprisonment up to 10 years

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (Independent Review or Audited) filed with CIPC (CoR 37.1 Annexure)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same anniversary window as annual return: within 30 business days after financial year-end when Public Interest Score >= 100
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Contravention of s33 Companies Act 2008; CIPC issues a compliance notice and may refer directors for civil or administrative sanction; failure to table AFS to shareholders is also a directors' delinquency ground under s162

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (ITR14) and Tax Reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after financial year-end (SARS assessed due date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late payment penalty on outstanding normal tax plus monthly interest of 10-12.5% per annum under s89bis/s89quat Income Tax Act 58 of 1962; administrative non-compliance penalty under the Tax Administration Act up to ZAR 16,000 (~USD 900) per month of non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Provisional Tax Second Return and Top-up Payment (IRP6 final reconciliation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Second provisional return due at the end of the financial year; top-up payment due by 15 October (non-September year-end) or 15 March (September year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under-estimation penalty under s163 Income Tax Act up to 20% of the understated taxable income; plus 10% late payment penalty and interest on any shortfall

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: The company computes its Public Interest Score (PIS) annually: 1 point per employee, 1 point per shareholder or trust beneficiary, 1 point per ZAR 1 million of third-party liabilities, and 1 point per ZAR 1 million of fiduciary assets; an independent review is mandatory when PIS = 100-349 and a full statutory audit when PIS >= 350, or at any PIS where the Memorandum of Incorporation so requires
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for SMEs for non-public interest companies; full IFRS for any company electing it or required by its MOI; financial statements must satisfy the fair presentation requirements of s29 Companies Act 2008 and conform to the Financial Reporting Standards as approved by the Financial Reporting Standards Council

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual BO confirmation is embedded in the CIPC annual return: the company must certify its beneficial owner(s) holding 25% or more beneficial ownership or control on the prescribed BO declaration; each share transfer must be recorded within 7 days by updating the BO register and the share register; a designated director or CIPC-accredited compliance officer lodges the declaration under penalty of a false-statements offence
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (share register) with transfer entries updated within 7 days
Register of Directors and Prescribed Officers
Beneficial Ownership Register (with 25%+ ultimate owner details)
Minute Book of general and director meetings
Memorandum of Incorporation and all amendment resolutions
Securities register and proxy documents for all issued shares

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $80-$260 (CIPC-accredited company secretarial and registered office services, excluding statutory audit)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $1,600-$4,500 for a full statutory audit; $800-$2,200 for an independent review where PIS = 100-349

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (applicable to companies with years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Section 11D R&D super-deduction (150%) for qualifying software research and development; accelerated capital allowances under Section 12C for computer and data-centre equipment; Section 12B allowances for renewable-energy and server-related assets; SEZ preferential rate of 15% is available only to qualifying companies physically operating inside a designated Special Economic Zone and is generally not available to a standard vertical-cloud (Pty) Ltd; no patent-box or IP exemption regime.
